'''Silvina Martha Ponce Dawson''' is an Argentine physicist specialized in [[biophysics]] and a full professor at the [[Faculty of Exact and Natural Sciences]] of the [[University of Buenos Aires]] (UBA), and senior researcher at the National Scientific Research Council ([[CONICET]]).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Silvina Ponce Dawson |url=https://council.science/profile/silvina-ponce-dawson-2/ |access-date=2025-01-20 |website=International Science Council |language=en-US}}</ref> In October 2024 she was elected to preside the [[International Union of Pure and Applied Physics]] (IUPAP) for the period 2025 to 2027.<ref>{{Cite web |last=iupap |date=2024-10-28 |title=Silvina Ponce Dawson IUPAP new President - IUPAP: The International Union of Pure and Applied Physics |url=https://iupap.org/2024/10/28/silvina-ponce-dawson-iupap-new-president/ |access-date=2025-01-20 |language=en-US}}</ref> Her main research interests are biological and statistical physics. She is the author of more than 100 articles that have appeared in scientific journals and conference proceedings.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Google Scholar citations for Silvina Ponce Dawson |url=https://accounts.google.com/v3/signin/identifier?continue=https%3A%2F%2Fscholar.google.com%2Fcitations%3Fview_op%3Dlist_works%26hl%3Den%26hl%3Den%26user%3D2NX8v24AAAA&hl=en&ifkv=AVdkyDleSI4mmbwj23kvblR66i3N0tB0Q5fpqnZ4AhTdzCdCdCx5J11oofy776Hum0f-EhnjZ7Uq&service=citations&flowName=GlifWebSignIn&flowEntry=ServiceLogin&dsh=S-383725394%3A1737389637216787&ddm=1 |access-date=2025-01-20 |website=accounts.google.com}}</ref>

== Research career ==
Silvina Ponce Dawson received the [[Licenciatura]] and [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] degrees in physics from the University of Buenos Aires, Argentina, in 1983 and 1988,<ref>{{Cite thesis |last=Ponce Dawson |first=Silvina |title=Un modelo de turbulencia de Alfven en plasmas |date=1988 |degree=PhD |publisher=Universidad de Buenos Aires. Facultad de Ciencias Exactas y Naturales |url=https://bibliotecadigital.exactas.uba.ar/collection/tesis/document/tesis_n2120_PonceDawson}}</ref> respectively.

She was a research assistant with the [[University of Maryland, College Park|University of Maryland]] from 1989 to 1991 and at the [[Los Alamos National Laboratory]] from 1991 to 1994. Ponce Dawson returned to the University of Buenos Aires in 1994 as an assistant professor, where she became full professor in 2017.<ref>{{Cite web |title=OpenReview |url=https://openreview.net/profile?id=~Silvina_Ponce_Dawson1 |access-date=2025-01-20 |website=OpenReview |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Silvina Ponce Dawson: Biography |url=https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/author/37089249775 |access-date=2025-01-20 |website=ieeexplore.ieee.org}}</ref>

Ponce Dawson is a research associate of the [[International Centre for Theoretical Physics|International Center for Theoretical Physics]] (ICTP) in Trieste, Italy,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Silvina Martha Ponce Dawson {{!}} ICTP |url=https://www.ictp.it/member/silvina-martha-ponce-dawson |access-date=2025-01-20 |website=www.ictp.it}}</ref> and an associate member of ICTP-SAIFR, Sao Paulo, Brazil.<ref>{{Cite web |title=ICTP – SAIFR » Associate Members |url=https://www.ictp-saifr.org/ictp-saifr-associate-members/ |access-date=2025-01-20 |website=www.ictp-saifr.org}}</ref> She is divisional associate editor of Physical Review Letters,<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-01-12 |title=Editors of Physical Review Letters |url=https://journals.aps.org/prl/staff |access-date=2025-01-20 |website=Physical Review Letters |language=en}}</ref> and she was a member of the Advisory Council of the National Program for Gender Equality of the Ministry of Science of Argentina (comité asesor del  Programa de Igualdad de Género del Ministerio de Ciencia de Argentina). She was director of the Faculty of Physics of the UBA from 2005 to 2009 and in charge of extension activities in the period between 2010 and 2016.

== International engagement ==
In October 2017, she was elected IUPAP vice-president at large,<ref>{{Cite web |date=2017-10-19 |title=Ponce Dawson a la IUPAP |url=https://exactas.uba.ar/ponce-dawson-a-la-iupap/ |access-date=2025-01-20 |website=Facultad de Ciencias Exactas y Naturales de la Universidad de Buenos Aires |language=es}}</ref> designate president in 2021, and finally president in 2024 for the period 2025 to 2027. Ponce Dawson was chair of the IUPAP [[Working Group on Women in Physics]] from 2011 to 2014, and the IUPAP gender champion from 2017 to 2019. She was member of the Executive Committee of the [[ICSU]]-funded Gender Gap in Science Project.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Chiu |first=Mei-Hung |last2=Cesa |first2=Mark |date=2020-07-01 |title=Gender Gap in Science: A Global Approach to the Gender Gap in Mathematical, Computing, and Natural Sciences: How to Measure it, How to Reduce It? |url=https://www.degruyter.com/document/doi/10.1515/ci-2020-0306/html |journal=Chemistry International |language=en |volume=42 |issue=3 |pages=16–21 |doi=10.1515/ci-2020-0306 |issn=1365-2192|doi-access=free }}</ref> She also co-edited a book on the gender gap in STEM in Latin America. She is a member of the advisory committee for the Program on Gender Equality of the Argentinian Ministry of Science.

Ponce Dawson is a member of the steering committee for the 2025 International Year of Quantum Science and Technology.
